items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: He looked at me with those eyes and said, 'young man, study Palestrina.'

ctx.x: He was a diminutive little man, Szegedi's blazing eyes. They were at Sagetti's apartment, rehearsing "Contrasty" and during an intermission I was introduced to Bartok, as a young composer, which I was. I was young anyway.
He didn't speak English very well. He looked at me with those eyes and said, "young man, study Palestrina." I tell that to everyone who is interested in writing, because I believe that.
If you look at what he did, he certainly did and if you look at what any of them did, they all did. There's no escaping it. The only time you don't sense that sort of thing is now.
